feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 9 & 0 \\ -4 & -8 & 0 \\ -6 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

If the matrix $A$ above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 9 & 0 \\ -4 & -8-\lambda  & 0 \\ -6 & -6 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 9 \\ -4 & -8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )((5-\lambda )(-8-\lambda )+36) & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -4) & =0 \\ -(\lambda +4)(\lambda +4)(\lambda -1) & =0 \\ (\lambda +4)^{2}(\lambda -1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=-4$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=1.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{1}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{1})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=-4.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{-4}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-(-4)I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-4)I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 9 & 0 \\ -4 & -8 & 0 \\ -6 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}]-(-4)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 9 & 0 \\ -4 & -4 & 0 \\ -6 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{3}+(\frac{4}{9}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -6 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(\frac{2}{3}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-4.$ So,

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{1})+\text{dim}({V}_{-4})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, a corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$
